SPOT- CRITIC2 Assessment Framework

SOURCE: Identifiable individuals associated with a state or non-state actor, cutouts, "bots", or a
third party such as a moderator. Can also be anonymous/unknown.
PLATFORM: TV, Radio, website, social media, print media, advertising platform, etc.
OBJECTIVE: The stated or implied goal of the language or image content used in an influence
operation.
TARGET: Intended audience of a campaign over a specific platform(s).
COMPOSITION: The specific language or image content used in an influence operation.
REACH:
• Category 1: Circulation on fringe websites, media outlets, or social media networks
• Category 2: Circulation on mainstream websites, media outlets, social media networks.
• Category 3: Break out across multiple media platforms, engagement by key audiences
or key opinion/decision makers
• Category 4: Widespread circulation on reputable media platforms, quoted by key
opinion/decision makers and eliciting a policy response
INFORMATION RESILIENCE:
• Category 1: Target has access to a limited number of independent media resources and
will have difficulty in developing an informed position.
• Category 2: Target has access to a variety of interdependent media sources from which
to inform their opinion.
THEME
• Category 1: Targets a single policy issue or activity, or capability, but does not credibly
undermine the mission orf core functions of USAID
• Category 2: Targets multiple policy issues, activities, or capabilities, but does not
credibly undermine the mission orf core functions of USAID

• Category 3: Targets one critical policy issues, activity, or capability and has a risk of
credibly undermininge the mission orf core functions bf USAID
• Category 4: Targets multiple critical issues, activities, or capabilities with a high risk of
credibility undermining the mission or core functions of USAID
INTERNAL RISK APPETITE:
• Low: Areas in which USAID avoids threats or acts to minimize or eliminate the likelihood
and/or impact that threats may occur.
• Medium: Areas in which USAID must continually strike a balance between opportunities
and threats.
• High: Areas in which USAID prefers evidence-based and disciplined risk taking.
CAMPAIGN:
A concerted effort (more than XX instances) by an adversary to spread MDM about a policy
issue or activity, or capability or attempts to credibility undermine the mission of core functions
of USAID
• Category 1: Yes
• Category 2: No
COMPETITOR
Presence of a strategic competitor in the country or region that seeks to undermine the mission
or core functions of USAID as a national policy objective (outside assessment).
• Category 1: Yes
• Category 2: No
IMPACT
Impact Determination
Level 1: Minor Impact
• Issue has little to no to affect on personnel security or efficacy of programs
